name: Table of Contents
description: A nested list of heading links that indents by heading level and highlights the section in view with an IntersectionObserver.
usage:
<TableOfContents
  headings={[
    { id: 'installation', level: 2, title: 'Installation' },
    { id: 'npm', level: 3, title: 'With npm' },
    { id: 'usage', level: 2, title: 'Usage' },
  ]}
/>

anatomy.description: Landmark labelled "Table of contents" by default.
Heading links indented by level into a nested outline.
The heading in view sets aria-current="location" via an IntersectionObserver.

dos: Pass headings in document order with their real levels.
Keep it in a side column on wide screens.
donts: Don't use it for flat section links; use Anchor Nav.
Don't fabricate levels; skipped levels still nest under the nearest ancestor.

examples.title: Nested by heading level
examples.description: A flat list of headings in document order becomes a nested, indented list; the observer tracks scrolling.

examples.title: Skipped levels
examples.description: Heading level gaps still nest under the nearest ancestor, so real documents stay correctly indented.

guidance.useWhen: Long-form content such as docs or articles needs an on-page outline that mirrors the heading hierarchy.
guidance.avoidWhen: The page has only flat sections with no hierarchy; use AnchorNav for a lighter flat list.
guidance.behavior: Clicking a link activates it and smooth-scrolls the heading into view; the IntersectionObserver moves aria-current as the reader scrolls, and activeId can be controlled.
guidance.responsive: Designed for a side column on wide screens; on narrow screens collapse it behind a disclosure or hide it entirely.

keyboard.action: Moves focus between the heading links.
Smooth-scrolls the linked heading into view and marks it active.

notes: Renders a navigation landmark labelled "Table of contents" with nested lists matching the heading hierarchy.
The active heading exposes aria-current="location" so the reading position is announced.
Without IntersectionObserver the links still navigate; only the scroll tracking is skipped.
